Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

account noun

a report of what happened

also narrative, report, retelling

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.80: rem narrāre ita ut vērīsimilis narrātiō sit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Or. 124 (Lewis & Short)

1narrātiō: short first a (Bennett’s nārrō). From narrō, which de Vaan (s.v. gnārus) derives from *nārāre, shortened by the littera-rule. Ruling: narrō with a short a.

narrātiō1, narrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an account, a telling of what happened

From narrō: any account of events; in rhetoric, the statement of the facts of a case.

Other words

  • expositiō, expositiōnis f. — a setting out of facts, an account

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 212: expositiōnēs rērum (Lewis & Short); Quint. 2.4.15 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • dīcere quae audierint ūtile est puerīs ad loquendī facultātem, ideōque et retrō agere expositiōnem et ā mediā in utramque partem discurrere

    retelling what they have heard is good for children’s speech; so let them tell the story backwards, and run from the middle to either endQuint. 2.4.15

See also accountability, demand an account, bank account, story, tell me what happened.

SourcesLewis & Short: narratio · Lewis & Short: expositio

Quintilian from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-quintilianus).
